sources.headline: Man charged with attack on Australia MP to face court
sources.text: Man charged with attack on Australia MP to face courtImage source, AFP via Getty ImagesImage caption, The community in Wangaratta remains in shock after the alleged attackByKaty WatsonAustralia correspondentReporting fromWangaratta, north-east Victoria and Phelan ChatterjeeA 43-year-old man has been charged after Australian MP Helen Haines was hit by a car in the state of Victoria on Monday.The suspect will appear in court on Wednesday to face charges of dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and the federal offence of causing harm to a public official.Local media earlier named the alleged attacker as environmental activist Brendan Nugent. His father and his partner said they had been friends with Haines "for more than 20 years" and thanked residents and officers who helped her after the "shocking and horrific crime". Haines remains in a critical condition after surgery and is reported to have lost one of her legs."Helen Haines is a deeply respected, valued and much loved member of our local community," Rod Nugent and his partner Christine Cunningham said in a statement."All of our love and all of our thoughts are with Helen and her family and friends."They promised to assist Victoria Police "in any way we can".Police say they will allege the incident was targeted.Haines, 65, the independent member for Indi, is in a critical but stable condition after undergoing surgery at a Melbourne hospital.Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Helen Haines sits as an independent MP for the electoral division of Indi in Australia's state of VictoriaShe was airlifted there after bystanders rushed to help.A local barber who was there says he pulled the suspect out of his car."I don't think I'm a hero. I think that I was just a person who had an opportunity to intervene in a safe-ish way," said Ricky Jefferies.Others who helped "didn't even check for danger", he added. "The car was still on and they sat in front of a rolling car, that's not an exaggeration."In their statement, Victoria Police say a highway patrol unit was nearby at the time of the incident and "on scene" within eight seconds of the call coming through.As they announced the charges against the 43-year-old, they said they had searched a property in Tarrawingee, around 12km (7.5 miles) from Wangaratta."At this stage it appears this is an isolated incident, and there are currently no other known threats connected to this matter," they said, adding officers would maintain a presence in Wangaratta.Haines won the seat of Indi as an independent in 2019, and has since become a prominent member of the crossbench, building rapport across Australia's increasingly divided political spectrum.The community, and country, remain in shock.At a vigil on Tuesday, locals queued patiently in the aisle of the Holy Trinity Cathedral, waiting for their turn to light a candle. Priests hugged some of those who came to pay their respects.Wangaratta's main street, where Haines's office is located, had reopened to traffic. Cars slowly filed past the growing number of bouquets being left for her on the pavement.One card read: "May you recover quickly and continue to be a light in this world."

Dozens of flowers and cards have been left for her in the hours since her attack, many in her signature orange.“To doctor Helen Haines, to show you some support you’ve shown us through difficult times,” one reads from the eastern region of Victoria police.Another, in child’s writing, says simply: “To Helen Haines, you’re very nice.”Hordes of cards and flowers have been left at Helen Haines’ electoral office. double quotation markThe purpose of setting them up was because of the increasing number of threats and the increasing number of reports that we’re receiving from parliamentarians and from their staff, but also our own proactive intelligence work in terms of identifying and addressing these threats and this type of communication, particularly in the online space.
AFP chief says one person charged every week for targeting parliamentariansThe Australian federal police commissioner, Krissy Barrett, says police are “charging almost one individual every week for targeting commonwealth parliamentarians or high office holders”.
double quotation markWhen it comes to federal parliamentarians, the AFP continues to record the growing volume of online abuse, threatening rhetoric, and intimidation, increasing political polarisation, and antigovernment sentiment, conspiracy-driven and grievance-based behaviours, lone actors motivated by a convergence of personal grievance, mental health vulnerabilities, and ideological concerns, and the potential for violence to emerge with little or no forewarning – particularly where individuals have no previous protection intelligence footprint.
Police considering further charges against alleged attackerThe chief commissioner of Victoria police, Mike Bush, has told reporters the 43-year-old charged over the alleged attack on Helen Haines was currently facing three charges: the commonwealth offence of causing harm to a commonwealth public official; and two state charges of intentionally causing serious harm, and dangerous driving causing serious harm.But Bush said police were considering further serious charges. He was asked directly whether the man could be charged with attempted murder.
double quotation markThat’s always a consideration. Of course, we have to locate and follow the evidence, but this is a very serious and tragic incident, and we will be looking at all serious charges.
But, of course, we have to have the evidence to support those charges.

double quotation markCertainly, it’s a reminder that the world is a more dangerous and divided place than it was a generation ago.
But I think that Australians do want to see their politicians be able to go about their business, to be able to get something from the back of their car, for goodness sake.
Speaking to ABC radio, the prime minister said “there’s no question” women in politics face more harassment than their male counterparts.
double quotation markMy side, every side included. We all have to recognise that politics has got more aggressive.
The particular impact on women in politics … [They] have got a different form of vilification and aggression towards them as well.
Cait KellyRegional Victorian community grapples with the unfathomableWangaratta remains in shock. The main street is quiet, aside from a large media throng outside Haines’ office. The front door is slowly being obscured by cards and flowers, as community members leave messages hoping for a quick recovery.On the streets, locals reflect the mood. They’re a tight-knit community where nothing like this happens. The shock is palpable. For the quiet regional city, it’s hard to comprehend.Helen Haines remains in critical condition, hospital saysThere has been no change to Helen Haines’s condition at the Alfred hospital in Melbourne. She “remains in a critical condition”, the hospital said Wednesday morning.Haines has lost one leg and surgeons operated Tuesday in an effort to save her other leg.“A further condition update will be shared late afternoon, when available,” the hospital said.Tess IkonomouDavid Pocock says security risks have caused him to move house several timesThe independent senator David Pocock has had to move house several times since being elected to federal parliament in 2022, over safety concerns.The former Wallabies captain told the Canberra Times the growing security risk threatened his young family.Security measures for parliamentarians and rising political violence are front and centre following the targeted attack against Helen Haines, which has left the Victorian MP with critical injuries.Pocock will address the National Press Club in Canberra on Wednesday for the first time in his political career.David Pocock. sources.headline: Australian Lawmaker Helen Haines Remains in Critical Condition After Car Attack
sources.text: Helen Haines, an independent, remained in critical condition after she was struck by a vehicle. A 43-year-old man was charged and will appear in court on Wednesday.

sources.headline: Australian MP seriously hurt in suspected car attack
sources.text:
An Australian lawmaker struck by a car in an apparently deliberate attack on Monday has lost one of her legs, local media reported, citing sources.
Independent MP Helen Haines underwent surgery overnight after suffering what were described as critical injuries in the incident, with national broadcaster ABC and the daily Sydney Morning Herald reporting on Tuesday that one leg had been amputated.
Counterterrorism investigators have joined a police probe into the incident, which occurred outside Haines' constituency office in Wangaratta, northeast of the Victorian capital, Melbourne.What do we know about the suspected attack on Haines?
Haines, 65, was hit by an SUV, which police said was a white Toyota, outside her office. She suffered serious injuries, particularly to her lower body.
ABC cited witnesses as saying they heard a bang and then saw a woman pinned between two cars.
The driver, described as a 43-year-old man, has been arrested, according to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.
Albanese said early investigations suggested the driver made a U-turn before hitting Haines as she was loading or unloading items at the trunk of her car.
"This wasn't an accident. There was a deliberate act, it would appear," he told ABC.
Local barber ran to assist
Local barber Ricky Jeffries, whose shop is next to Haines' office, has been widely hailed as a hero after he ran to pull the driver out of the car and restrained him until police arrived.Barber Ricky Jefferies has been called a hero for restraining the driverImage: Seven Network/REUTERS
Jeffries downplayed his role, despite having intervened in what could have been a highly dangerous situation, as the man had a knife in the car.
"He [the driver] did have a knife. He didn't ​pull it ‌out. I just wasn't comfortable with his movements, and so I basically just took it out of his pocket and threw it away," he said.
Jefferies said he then held the man down until ‌police arrived.
"I just leant over him and once he was on the ground and ‌he was ​no longer a threat, I just stood with him and I told him that he can't leave," he said.
Jefferies told journalists his first thought had been: "My wife would be disappointed if I'm injured."
"The other people here were just, they did so much more than me ... they deserve the credit," he added.
Political violence on the rise: PM Albanese
Albanese said it was too early to speculate about the possible motive behind the suspected attack, but pointed to rising political violence.
"The temperature has increased in recent times," Albanese added, "I've expressed that concern to people in the media."Prime Minister Albanese has said the incident seemed 'no accident'Image: Marek Ladzinski/ZUMA/picture alliance
Ben Carroll, the state premier for Victoria where Wangaratta is located, said he was "appalled" by the attack, adding: "I know how devastating this will be for the Wangaratta community and all those who Helen represents."
At a separate press conference, Albanese said everyone was "praying for her full recovery."
Although it has not yet been established whether the incident was deliberate, there has been an increase in threats and harassment targeting lawmakers and other senior public officials in Australia and elsewhere in recent years.
Haines had worked as a nurse and a midwife before entering parliament in 2019. She is known for her stance on stronger climate action.
Edited by: Karl Sexton and Louis Oelofse

sources.headline: Australian prime minister says lawmaker critically injured by car is 'no accident'
sources.text:
Australian independent member of parliament Helen Haines speaks to journalists in the Press Gallery at Parliament House in Canberra, Australia, Tuesday, Sept. 8, 2026.
Mick Tsikas/AAP Image via AP
hide caption
Mick Tsikas/AAP Image via AP
MELBOURNE, Australia — A car hit an Australian federal independent lawmaker on Monday, critically injuring her in an apparent deliberate attack, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said. The driver was arrested. Helen Haines, 65, was struck by a Toyota Land Cruiser SUV outside her electoral district office mid afternoon in the city of Wangaratta in Victoria state, a police said. Albanese said the national counterterrorism team, incorporating police and intelligence agencies, was investigating. "This wasn't an accident. There was a deliberate act, it would appear. We don't know what the motivation is," Albanese told Australian Broadcasting Corp.
Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese speaks to Independent member of parliament, Helen Haines, in the House of Representatives at Parliament House in Canberra, Australia, Tuesday, Aug. 18, 2026.
Lukas Coch/AAPIMAGE via AP
hide caption
Lukas Coch/AAPIMAGE via AP
The 43-year-old driver was arrested at the scene by a passerby. He will be interviewed in relation to the incident, police said.
"A knife was located by police and seized from inside the Toyota," police said. "At this stage, police are investigating as to whether this was an intentional act," police added. Haines, who was first elected to the Parliament in 2019, was taken to a hospital with critical injuries, police said. The episode has renewed safety concerns for Australian lawmakers, in a country where politicians have historically been highly accessible to the public and usually go about their business without security officers present. But public incitement against officials is growing. Australian Federal Police Commissioner Krissy Barrett said in 2025 that threats against parliamentarians had doubled over the past three years. Police data showed more than 1,000 such threats against politicians in the 2025-2026 financial year, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said Monday. Albanese told the ABC it was "unfortunate" that an increasingly polarized political climate had already led to security changes for Australia's lawmakers. "I think there has been a rise in temperature and there has been too much shouting, not enough discourse, not enough polite conversation and disagreement," he said Monday. There was "no question" that social media played a part, Albanese added. In Britain, murders of politicians have prompted bolstered security. Labour lawmaker Jo Cox was shot and stabbed in 2016 by a far-right extremist, and Conservative David Amess was stabbed in 2021 by an attacker inspired by the Islamic State group.
In July, the former politician and reality TV contestant Ann Widdecombe was found slain with a hammer at her home. A man has been charged with murder and terrorism-related offenses.

sources.headline: Police not ruling out further serious charges over Helen Haines attack
sources.text: Further serious charges may be laid against a Victorian man over his alleged attack on Indi MP Helen Haines on Monday.Brendan Nugent, 43, has been charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and causing harm to a Commonwealth public official.Ms Haines, 65, remains in hospital in a critical but stable condition.Victoria Police and the Australian Federal Police (AFP) told a press conference this morning they have not ruled out laying further charges, including attempted murder."While I say this investigation is far from complete, we are not ruling out further serious charges," Victoria Police Chief Commissioner Mike Bush said."I want to further add that we have deployed a number of staff into Wangaratta to give assurance to members of the public."We do believe this was a deliberate but isolated act."Chief Commissioner Bush said there were no "intelligence holdings" against Mr Nugent and police had no information to suggest he was an "immediate threat". Helen Haines remains in a critical but stable condition in hospital. (AAP: Mick Tsikas)Details of Mr Nugent's previous brushes with the law have emerged since he was arrested on Monday.He was charged with breaching an interim personal safety intervention order in July 2022 at Tarrawingee, where he lives.The case went to the Wangaratta Magistrates' Court.Court records show the charges were dismissed in December, 2022 and the matter was finalised.Brendan Nugent is facing three charges over the alleged attack on Helen Haines. (X)Mr Nugent appears to be a long-time resident in Ms Haines's electorate.In a statement yesterday, Mr Nugent's family said they were long-time friends of Ms Haines."Helen has been our friend for more than 20 years and what happened to her yesterday is devastating and unfathomable," father Rod Nugent and Rod's partner Christine Cunningham said in a statement."All of our love and all of our thoughts are with Helen and her family and friends."ABC Verify revealed that Mr Nugent posted to social media regularly for more than a decade about the environment and politics.A neighbour told the ABC that they had called the police on him numerous times, and sources have confirmed that he has undergone a mental health assessment following the alleged attack.Chief Commissioner Bush said police would investigate whether the 43-year-old was involved in the sovereign citizen movement or whether the attack was personal."His motivation for this, what we allege is a deliberate attack, is very much a centrepiece of the investigation," he said."That's obviously something we're exploring."We haven't had any direct evidence of that … But we're not ruling it out."Two police officers were killed in nearby Porepunkah in August last year by self-proclaimed "sovereign citizen" Dezi Freeman.Chief Commissioner Bush said Ms Haines had been a huge support to local officers and the community during that time."She gave wonderful support to local police, and I know that my colleagues there absolutely appreciate what she did and continues to do for them," he said.Local officers swiftly attended the scene at Wangaratta on Monday, Chief Commissioner Bush said."Our officers in Wangaratta arrived on that traumatic scene within seconds, in fact I think it was 8 seconds," he said."Their actions prevented further serious harm to Helen."Ms Haines lost a leg following the incident and surgeons at Melbourne's Alfred Hospital are still fighting to save her other leg.People were seen sobbing outside a church in Wangaratta after a vigil for Helen Haines on Tuesday. (ABC News: Nate Woodall)Unlawful behaviour towards MPs increasingAFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett said authorities had been seeing an increase in unlawful behaviour towards parliamentarians, with "almost one individual every week" charged for targeting Commonwealth officials."I hope that this terrible event — that will forever change the life of the member for Indi and her family — gives our country time to pause and reflect on the growing threats and unlawful behaviour against those who hold a Commonwealth office in Australia," she said.Victoria Police said it would leverage its state command and coordination centre to ensure it was across further political threats."Especially leading up to the election, against any politicians in this state, to make sure there is a centralised place of reporting, a place where we can proactively search for any threats and ensure that we act quickly and we act proactively," Chief Commissioner Bush said.

sources.headline: Man charged in "targeted" attack on Australian lawmaker Helen Haines
sources.text:
October 20, 2026 / 9:51 AM EDT
/ CBS/AFP
Add CBS News on Google
Australian police charged a man on Tuesday over what they alleged was a "targeted" attack with a vehicle on independent lawmaker Helen Haines.Haines has reportedly lost one of her legs in the aftermath of the incident on Monday afternoon, in which a car rammed into her multiple times as she stood near the trunk of her own parked vehicle in the southeastern city of Wangaratta, according to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation.Authorities said the 65-year-old was getting something from the back of her car when her alleged attacker drove past in a Toyota Land Cruiser. He allegedly turned the car around before veering into Haines, pinning her against her own vehicle and then reversing before ramming into her again, according to local authorities and Australian Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke. Brendan Nugent, from nearby Tarrawingee, was charged with intentionally causing serious injury, dangerous driving causing serious injury and causing harm to a federal official, police said in a statement on Tuesday.
A photo of independent member of parliament Helen Haines is shown on the window of her electoral office in Wangaratta, Australia, Tuesday, Oct. 20, 2026.
James Ross/AAPImage via AP
Police have said little about the suspect's potential motive, but they have characterized the incident as a "deliberate" act of violence. Political violence is historically uncommon across Australia, though data show threats have grown in recent years.Suspect to face court on WednesdayNugent has been in police custody since shortly after Haines was injured and a crowd of bystanders subdued him. He will appear in a Wangaratta court on Wednesday, when he could potentially be released on bail.
His father, Rod Nugent, released a statement Tuesday describing Haines as a "deeply respected, valued and much-loved member of our local community." "Helen has been our friend for more than 20 years and what happened to her yesterday is devastating and unfathomable," the father said, adding that he would cooperate with police."Absolutely devastated"Wangaratta Mayor Irene Grant said a somber mood had settled over the town of about 30,000 people, a regional hub about 250 kilometers, or 155 miles, northeast of state capital Melbourne."Helen was well-respected. She was diligent and hard working," Grant told AFP. "What has happened to Helen has caused the community to step back in utter disbelief. We can't believe it, people are horrified by what has happened."
Locals, meanwhile, are struggling to comprehend why anyone would wish harm on the well-liked Haines.Florist Jess Woodrow said Haines was a friendly face who would pop into the store when she was not tied up in the capital Canberra."We are absolutely devastated to hear what has happened. Helen was a beautiful person. She didn't have a bad bone in her body," Woodrow told AFP. "It's the last thing you would think would happen here."Haines entered parliament as an independent lawmaker in 2019, representing the sprawling seat of Indi. Her popularity led to her holding the seat in the 2025 election, with a hefty margin of more than 18,000 votes.Haines was a vocal champion for greater climate action, better rural healthcare, and help for struggling small businesses, while the First Peoples' Assembly of Victoria said Haines was a "staunch supporter" of Indigenous rights as well. But it was her work to hold politicians to account that perhaps earned Haines the most respect both inside and outside parliament."Helen Haines is characterized by her kindness, her compassion, her diligence, her intelligence," Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said. "She's someone who is such a strong advocate and is widely respected right across the political spectrum because the way that she advocates is very respectful."
